items.title: Ray Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, AZ, April 16, 2000
items.q: He gave people the very best musicians... he always had top people playing for him... I remember we would finish a tour... he'd say, 'Okay, one take.'

ctx.x: There was one, something about Bill Harris who purposely knocked over something when Oscar was trying to sing or something like that?

Yeah but that was the backlash of something that happened before. We were in Japan and we used to have something called a Ballad Medley. The Ballad Medley was everybody playing one chorus of whatever ballad he chose to play. So what they did is they would black out the stage, put a spotlight just in the front at the microphone. The first guy would walk out, he would walk past Oscar and he’d say “’I’ve Got It Bad’ B flat” and then he’d © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

walk over. As he’s walking to the mic Oscar would do a four or eight bar introduction. He’d play one chorus. And then as he’s walking off to applause, the next guy walked by and Oscar would say so-and-so-and-so. And that’s the Ballad Medley. Okay. Now all of these tricks and stuff are still going on. I used to lay my bass on the stage, because we’d have a break at intermission, and then we would start the second half with Ella Fitzgerald. So they would call Buddy Rich, Herb Ellis, Ray Brown, Oscar Peterson, and…
